steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time on that date (PT is still on daylight saving time, so it’s PDT).  
Friday at 11:59 PM PT is Saturday morning in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is on Pacific Daylight Time on October 30, 2026, which is UTC−7. Madrid is on Central European Summer Time, UTC+2, so Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles.

So Monday at 10:00 AM in Los Angeles is Monday at 7:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts at 2026-10-24 18:00 in Madrid and lasts exactly 48 hours, so it ends two days later at the same local clock time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The final round starts on **2026-10-26 at 10:00 AM PT**. On that date, Pacific Time is on daylight saving time (**PDT, UTC−7**).  
So the deadline is **72 hours later**, which is **2026-10-29 at 10:00 AM PT**.

Madrid is on **CEST (UTC+2)** on October 29, 2026, so that converts to **7:00 PM** local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 19:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET is November 1, 2026 at 04:59 in Madrid time if Madrid is on CET/CEST? Let’s account carefully:

- On October 31, 2026, New York is on EDT (UTC-4), so 11:59 PM ET = 03:59 UTC on November 1.
- Add 36 hours = 15:59 UTC on November 2.
- Madrid on November 2, 2026 is on CET (UTC+1), so that is 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp **1791788340** corresponds to **2026-08-12 15:39:00 UTC**. Tokyo is **UTC+9**, so the local time is **2026-08-13 00:39**.

ANSWER: 2026-08-13 00:39 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) on 2026-10-25, so the UTC deadline is 2 hours later locally.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 04:30 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25, 2026.  
At that date, Pacific Time is on standard time (PST, UTC−8), while Madrid is on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), so Madrid is 9 hours ahead.

So 11:59 PM Pacific Time on that day is 8:59 AM in Madrid on the next day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the U.S. ends daylight saving time on Sunday, November 1, at 2:00 a.m. Eastern Time. So the contest deadline is **12:00 noon Eastern Time** on that day.

Lima, Peru is on **UTC-5** year-round, while Eastern Time is **UTC-5** during standard time after DST ends. So the deadline is the same clock time in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE means “Anywhere on Earth,” which is UTC−12. So December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE is the same as January 1, 2027, 12:00 UTC, which in Tokyo (UTC+9) is 21:00 on January 1, 2027.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is on AEDT on October 5, 2026 (UTC+11).  
So 5:00 PM in Sydney corresponds to 4:00 AM in New York on the same date, October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 04:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).
